response_change.parent_relation: For fixed A and parameters, dV_dt depends affinely on V through a constant leak slope -leak_conductance/membrane_capacitance, so the passive restoring force grows linearly with depolarization from resting_voltage.
response_change.child_relation: Replace constant linear leak with a voltage-dependent passive restoration that becomes steeper at larger depolarization from resting_voltage, so dV_dt vs V acquires state-dependent curvature while preserving outward restorative sign.
response_change.observable_effect: Under stronger sustained depolarization, the instantaneous voltage derivative bends downward more sharply than a single linear leak predicts, producing stronger compression of depolarized trajectories and a lower driven subthreshold plateau than expected from extrapolating weak-drive behavior.

plan.activation_condition: Observable when sustained applied_current is large enough that V remains appreciably above resting_voltage for times comparable to or longer than adaptation_time_constant, yet still below spike threshold; near-rest excursions the refinement is weak and the parent is approximately recovered.
plan.train_hidden_contrast: In training, moderate depolarizations already reveal slight sublinear growth of attainable V with applied_current. In holdout, stronger but still subthreshold depolarization extends this same effect into clearer downward curvature of dV_dt versus V, rather than introducing a different regime.
plan.continuation_path: In the limit of vanishing voltage dependence of the passive conductance, or for trajectories confined close to V = resting_voltage, the child reduces continuously to the parent linear-leak law.
plan.gap_statement: The model assumes a strictly Ohmic passive membrane current with one constant leak conductance across the full subthreshold range, omitting common voltage-dependent subthreshold rectification.
plan.baseline_assumption: Membrane capacitance and passive conductance are constant.
plan.scientific_mechanism: Subthreshold voltage-dependent leak/rectifying membrane conductance that increases outward restorative current during larger depolarizations.
plan.rationale: A realistic next refinement is to relax the constant-leak assumption rather than add a new process. The parent target mapping has a single fixed slope in V: after accounting for A, every depolarized trajectory follows the same linear passive restoration strength. Hold leak_conductance, membrane_capacitance, adaptation_gain, and adaptation_time_constant fixed while varying applied_current over weak versus stronger sustained depolarizing drives. The parent with one shared parameter set predicts that the passive V-dependence of dV_dt is the same straight line in both conditions; only the offset through applied_current and the induced A trajectory change. A child with voltage-dependent passive restoration changes the target mapping itself: at larger depolarization above resting_voltage, dV_dt becomes more negative than linear extrapolation from near-rest behavior, yielding curvature in the V-to-dV_dt relation and stronger saturation of subthreshold voltage under stronger drive. This is scientifically admissible in the stated subthreshold regime and does not rely on unsampled spike events. The effect is most visible when V is maintained above rest long enough for adaptation to coexist with appreciable depolarization; if trajectories stay near rest, the parent remains a good approximation, which is an explicit limitation.

plan.activation_condition: Observable during sustained depolarizing steps that keep the cell subthreshold yet several millivolts above resting_voltage for a duration comparable to the slow capacitance-relaxation timescale; weak or brief perturbations recover the parent-like fixed-capacitance behavior.
plan.train_hidden_contrast: In training, stronger sustained depolarization already yields slower late charging than early charging; in holdout, longer or slightly stronger subthreshold steps extend the same history-dependent phase shift rather than introducing a new mechanism.
plan.continuation_path: Capacitance-relaxation gain tending to zero, or capacitance-relaxation time constant tending to zero with the state pinned to the baseline membrane_capacitance, recovers the parent law.
plan.promotion_reason: A fixed capacitance cannot represent slow dielectric/electrotonic recruitment or voltage-dependent membrane area participation that changes the instantaneous dV_dt mapping over time under constant drive; the parameter must evolve as a state to create this observable phase dependence.
plan.gap_statement: The model assumes membrane_capacitance is constant, omitting slow activity-dependent changes in effective capacitance or electrotonic loading during sustained subthreshold depolarization.
plan.baseline_assumption: Membrane capacitance and passive conductance are constant.
plan.scientific_mechanism: Slow depolarization-dependent recruitment of effective membrane capacitance, representing gradual engagement of additional membrane area or gating charge that increases charge storage during sustained subthreshold drive.
plan.rationale: Parent response relationship: with constant applied_current and shared parameters fixed, dV_dt at any moment is net_drive divided by one constant membrane_capacitance, so apart from evolving A and leak terms there is no separate slow charging phase from the denominator itself. Planned child change: keep the same restorative currents but allow effective capacitance to increase slowly with depolarization, so the target mapping from observed states to dV_dt changes over time even under constant applied_current. Distinguishing condition: vary sustained applied_current amplitude across subthreshold step protocols while holding initial conditions V=-65 and A=0 and all other parameters fixed. Then compare early versus later portions of the voltage trajectory at matched V above rest. The child predicts stronger current steps produce a larger late reduction in dV_dt than can be explained by A alone because the charging denominator has also increased; the parent has only a single charging phase and one fixed capacitance, so one shared refit cannot simultaneously match both the early rapid rise and the later slowed charging across multiple step amplitudes if this history-dependent denominator effect is present. This is scientifically admissible when depolarization is sustained long enough for slow capacitance recruitment but remains subthreshold; if stimuli are too weak, too brief, or all observations are confined to very early times, the refinement may be hard to distinguish.

plan.train_hidden_contrast: In training, increasing depolarization already recruits larger A and leak rectification; in holdout, the same subthreshold regime extends to stronger sustained depolarization where equal A values produce a larger suppressive effect on dV_dt than the parent's voltage-independent additive adaptation can capture with one shared parameter set.
plan.continuation_path: Recover the parent law when the voltage dependence of adaptation current is taken to zero, yielding a purely additive subtraction of A from the numerator of dV_dt.
plan.gap_statement: The current model treats the adaptation variable as an ideal current source whose instantaneous effect on voltage is independent of membrane voltage, although many subthreshold adaptation mechanisms act more like voltage-dependent outward conductances with a driving force relative to a reversal potential.
plan.baseline_assumption: Adaptation enters the membrane equation as a voltage-independent hyperpolarizing current -A.
plan.scientific_mechanism: Subthreshold adaptation channels often generate outward current proportional to both a slow activation variable and the membrane driving force, making adaptation efficacy increase with depolarization even before spiking.
plan.rationale: A realistic next refinement is to relax the ideal-current assumption for adaptation rather than add an unrelated process. Hold applied_current, leak_conductance, adaptation kinetics, and baseline_membrane_capacitance fixed, and compare trajectories or sampled states with the same nonzero A but different subthreshold V. In the parent, the target mapping changes with A only by a constant vertical shift of -A/membrane_capacitance, independent of V. In the child, adaptation exerts stronger suppression of dV_dt at larger depolarization because outward current scales with driving force, so the A effect is no longer a constant shift but a V-dependent interaction. This is scientifically admissible in sustained depolarization regimes where adaptation has recruited and the neuron remains below threshold. The contrast concerns the scored target mapping itself, not merely auxiliary A trajectories: even if observed A were held fixed, dV_dt would differ as a function of V. A single refit of existing parent parameters cannot reproduce this across conditions with equal A at different V because the parent's partial derivative with respect to A is fixed at -1/membrane_capacitance, whereas the child makes that slope vary with depolarization. Near rest or when A remains near zero, the refinement becomes hard to observe, which is an honest limitation.

plan.activation_condition: Visible when applied_current is large enough to keep V moderately above resting_voltage for times comparable to or longer than the adaptation time scale, but still below spike threshold, so slow cumulative gating changes can develop without leaving the subthreshold regime.
plan.train_hidden_contrast: The same sustained-depolarization protocol that reveals saturating recruitment of A in training can also reveal a later weakening of adaptation efficacy during longer or slightly stronger holdout depolarizations; the mechanism extends the same subthreshold drive regime rather than requiring new interventions.
plan.continuation_path: Recover the parent by taking the added availability process infinitely fast and fixed at full availability, or by setting its voltage dependence to zero so adaptation efficacy remains the original static function of V - adaptation_reversal_voltage.
plan.promotion_reason: A history-dependent loss of adaptation efficacy cannot be represented with the existing states because A currently encodes only recruited adaptation magnitude and membrane_capacitance affects charging rather than adaptation-channel availability; an additional slow state is needed to store cumulative permissive inactivation or depletion.
plan.gap_statement: The current model assumes adaptation efficacy depends only on instantaneous driving force and adaptation magnitude, omitting slow use-dependent reduction of the outward adaptation mechanism during sustained subthreshold depolarization.
plan.baseline_assumption: The voltage dependence of adaptation efficacy is memoryless and has no slow permissive/inactivating gate beyond A itself.
plan.scientific_mechanism: Slow subthreshold inactivation or availability loss of adaptation-channel conductance, causing adaptation current efficacy to weaken after prolonged depolarization even while the recruited adaptation variable remains elevated.
plan.rationale: A realistic next refinement is to relax the parent's single-phase assumption for the adaptation contribution to dV_dt. In the parent, once applied_current is fixed, the scored target mapping depends on V, A, and membrane_capacitance with adaptation efficacy determined only by the instantaneous driving force. Thus, for a given observed V and A, the parent predicts the same adaptation-induced outward slope contribution regardless of whether the cell just depolarized or has been held depolarized for a long time. A plausible child adds a slow availability state for the adaptation pathway, so prolonged depolarization can reduce effective outward current despite A remaining high. The concrete distinguishing condition is to compare two times within sustained constant-current responses while holding applied_current and all parameters fixed: an early depolarized epoch shortly after A has risen versus a later epoch after prolonged subthreshold depolarization. In the child, dV_dt at similar V and A can become less negative later because adaptation efficacy has declined; in the parent, one shared parameter set cannot produce this history-dependent phase shift because the mapping from supplied states to dV_dt is memoryless in adaptation efficacy. This effect is scientifically admissible in a subthreshold regime with moderate sustained depolarization lasting long enough for slow inactivation, and it disappears in the limit of negligible or frozen availability dynamics.

response_change.parent_relation: The adaptation current contributes instantaneously to dV_dt through a static saturating function of the instantaneous driving force V - adaptation_reversal_voltage, so for fixed V and A the outward adaptation efficacy is single-phase and memoryless.
response_change.child_relation: Adaptation efficacy is filtered by a slow permissive inactivation or availability state, so the effective A-to-dV_dt coupling depends on both present voltage and prior sustained depolarization, creating a delayed reduction of outward adaptation impact during prolonged subthreshold drive.
response_change.observable_effect: Under the same constant applied_current and identical initial conditions, moderate sustained depolarization can show early strong adaptation-mediated slowing followed by partial recovery of dV_dt later in the trajectory as adaptation-channel availability declines; the parent only supports a single monotone settling phase once A rises.

diagnostic_groups.name: depolarization_above_rest
diagnostic_groups.role: Subthreshold depolarizing regime that recruits slow adaptation-related gating processes

diagnostic_groups.name: adaptation_drive_force
diagnostic_groups.role: Instantaneous electrical driving force for the outward adaptation current

diagnostic_groups.name: adaptation_effective_coupling
diagnostic_groups.role: Parent memoryless adaptation contribution to membrane-voltage slope

contract.activation_condition: Visible when applied_current is large enough to keep V moderately above resting_voltage for times comparable to or longer than the adaptation time scale, but still below spike threshold, so slow cumulative gating changes can develop without leaving the subthreshold regime.
contract.train_hidden_contrast: The same sustained-depolarization protocol that reveals saturating recruitment of A in training can also reveal a later weakening of adaptation efficacy during longer or slightly stronger holdout depolarizations; the mechanism extends the same subthreshold drive regime rather than requiring new interventions.
contract.continuation_path: Recover the parent by taking the added availability process infinitely fast and fixed at full availability, or by setting its voltage dependence to zero so adaptation efficacy remains the original static function of V - adaptation_reversal_voltage.
contract.promotion_reason: A history-dependent loss of adaptation efficacy cannot be represented with the existing states because A currently encodes only recruited adaptation magnitude and membrane_capacitance affects charging rather than adaptation-channel availability; an additional slow state is needed to store cumulative permissive inactivation or depletion.
contract.scientific_mechanism: Slow subthreshold inactivation or availability loss of adaptation-channel conductance, causing adaptation current efficacy to weaken after prolonged depolarization even while the recruited adaptation variable remains elevated.
contract.difficulty_rationale: This embedding introduces a distinct slow timescale that stores prior depolarization history and multiplicatively modulates an existing nonlinear current term, so the target mapping cannot be reproduced by a coefficient-only change in the memoryless adaptation law.
contract.assumption_before: The current model assumes adaptation efficacy depends only on instantaneous driving force and adaptation magnitude, omitting slow use-dependent reduction of the outward adaptation mechanism during sustained subthreshold depolarization.
contract.assumption_after: Adaptation efficacy is additionally controlled by a slow depolarization-dependent availability state that reduces current efficacy after prolonged subthreshold depolarization.
contract.before_fragment: (applied_current - leak_conductance*(1 + leak_rectification_strength*(V - resting_voltage)**2)*(V - resting_voltage) - A*(V - adaptation_reversal_voltage)*adaptation_conductance_saturation_scale/((V - adaptation_reversal_voltage) + adaptation_conductance_saturation_scale))/membrane_capacitance
contract.after_fragment: (applied_current - leak_conductance*(1 + leak_rectification_strength*(V - resting_voltage)**2)*(V - resting_voltage) - G*A*(V - adaptation_reversal_voltage)*adaptation_conductance_saturation_scale/((V - adaptation_reversal_voltage) + adaptation_conductance_saturation_scale))/membrane_capacitance
contract.parent_reduction: Set adaptation_inactivation_gain = 0 so the G target is 1, or equivalently let adaptation_availability_time_constant -> 0 with full-availability target; then G = 1 and the parent expression is recovered.
contract.observable_signature: Compare early and late epochs of the same sustained subthreshold current step while applied_current and parameters are held fixed. At similar V and A reached later in the trajectory, the child predicts a less negative adaptation contribution and partial recovery of dV_dt because G has declined, whereas the parent predicts the same adaptation contribution whenever V and A match.
contract.shortcut_blocked: A single refit of the parent parameters cannot reproduce this contrast because the parent target mapping from supplied states (V, A, membrane_capacitance) to dV_dt is memoryless in adaptation efficacy: if V and A are similar at two times, the parent must output nearly the same adaptation term. The child adds an independent hidden state G that separates early and late depolarized epochs without changing the observed protocol, so coefficient retuning alone cannot generate the required history-dependent phase shift across those conditions.
